checklist.step: Register the incident and stamp the awareness time
actions: Take the alert from the SOC Analyst on duty or the service desk and open an Incident record in ServiceNow with category ICT / Operational.

Enter the awareness timestamp in UTC in the Detected field - this is the start of the 24-hour outer limit, so take it from the first monitoring alert or first user report, not from the time you opened the ticket.
Populate Affected CIs from the CMDB, the business services behind them, and whether an ICT third-party provider is in the chain.
Set Priority P1/P2 and add the Operational Risk Manager and Operational Resilience Lead as watchers so the classification clock starts with them, not at the post-incident review.
checklist.done: the incident record carries a UTC awareness timestamp, affected CIs and business services, and the Operational Risk Manager is on the record.

checklist.step: Score the incident against the major-incident classification criteria
actions: Open the Major Incident Classification worksheet in the GRC platform and pull the incident id from ServiceNow.

Score each criterion with the measured value, not an opinion: clients and financial counterparties affected and transactions affected (counts and % of total), reputational impact, duration and service downtime in hours, geographical spread across Member States, data losses (availability, authenticity, integrity, confidentiality), criticality of services affected, and economic impact in EUR (direct and indirect costs).
Get the client and transaction counts from the Data Quality Manager as a query against the enterprise data warehouse rather than a business estimate.
Record which thresholds are met and whether the combination triggers major status; attach the query outputs as the evidence line for each criterion.
checklist.done: every classification criterion has a measured value, a source query and a met/not-met flag on the worksheet.

checklist.step: Confirm the major classification and start the 4-hour notification clock
actions: Review the scored worksheet with the Operational Resilience Analyst and take the major / not-major decision within the same working session - a deferred decision does not stop the 24-hour outer limit running.
Where the answer is major, stamp the Classification timestamp in UTC on the GRC record; the initial notification is then due 4 hours later and in any case within 24 hours of the awareness timestamp.
Call the Chief Risk Officer to confirm the call and record their confirmation on the record; where they disagree, log the reason and the final decision.
Where the answer is not major, write the reason against each unmet criterion so the decision can be re-performed later, and flag the incident for recurrence aggregation.
checklist.done: a dated, attributed major / not-major decision exists with the classification timestamp and the two derived deadlines showing on the record.

checklist.step: Assemble the initial notification data fields
actions: Open the major-incident notification form in the Internal Regulatory System and select the lead NCA and the reporting entity LEI.

Complete the initial-report block: incident reference, date and time of detection and of classification, description, whether the incident originated at an ICT third-party provider, Member States affected, and whether the incident is suspected to be malicious.
Pull the affected-service list from the Incident Response Lead and the client/transaction counts from the classification worksheet so the two documents cannot disagree.
Leave unknown fields explicitly marked as not yet available rather than guessing - the intermediate report is the place to complete them.
checklist.done: the initial notification form is complete against the classification worksheet with every unknown field flagged as pending.

checklist.step: Submit the initial notification inside the 4-hour / 24-hour window
actions: Check the submission clock on the record before sending: not later than 4 hours after classification and not later than 24 hours after awareness, whichever falls first.
Submit the form to the NCA through the supervisory reporting channel and capture the acknowledgement id, submission timestamp and the receiving authority on the incident record.
Where the channel is unavailable, use the NCA's documented fallback (secure email to the named supervisory contact) and record the fallback used, the time and the reason.
Notify the Chief Risk Officer and the Compliance Officer that the initial notification is filed, with the acknowledgement id.
checklist.done: an NCA acknowledgement id and submission timestamp are on the record and the submission timestamp is inside both statutory windows.

checklist.step: Check ICT third-party involvement and drive the provider's own reporting
actions: Identify from the CMDB and the register of information which outsourced or ICT service sits in the incident chain and whether it supports a critical or important function.
Open the contract in the contract lifecycle management repository and read the incident notification clause: notice period, content and the provider's obligation to support regulatory reporting.
Demand from the provider a written incident statement with their detection time, root cause and remediation, and set the due date to at least 24 hours before our intermediate report is due.
Where the provider misses the contractual notice period, raise a vendor issue with the Vendor Manager and record it as an input to the next annual provider assessment.
checklist.done: the provider's written incident statement is on file ahead of the intermediate report, or a vendor issue is raised for its absence.

checklist.step: File the intermediate report within 72 hours
actions: Reopen the notification form and complete the intermediate block: current status, whether regular activities have been recovered, the temporary actions taken, and updated client, transaction and downtime figures.
Re-run the classification queries with the Data Quality Manager so the updated impact numbers are measured at the 72-hour point rather than carried forward from the initial report.
Restate the economic impact in EUR splitting direct costs (recovery, replacement, third-party fees) from indirect (lost revenue, penalties) and show the basis of the estimate.
Submit before the 72-hour mark from the initial notification and record the second acknowledgement id.
checklist.done: the intermediate report is submitted inside 72 hours with refreshed impact measures and an acknowledgement id.

checklist.step: Establish root cause and the remediation plan
actions: Run the post-incident review with the SOC Lead, the affected service owner and the Third-Party Risk Manager within 5 working days of service restoration.
Record the root cause against a fixed taxonomy (change failure, capacity, configuration, third-party outage, malicious act, process failure) and attach the supporting log evidence from the SIEM.
Raise a problem record per corrective action with an owner and a due date, and link every problem record back to the incident id.
Hand the agreed root cause and action list to the Operational Risk Manager for the final regulatory report.
checklist.done: a root cause from the taxonomy, evidenced from logs, with linked problem records each carrying an owner and due date.

checklist.step: File the final report within one month
actions: Complete the final block of the notification form: root cause, the full chronology from detection to restoration, permanent corrective actions and their dates, final direct and indirect costs, and recurring-incident information.
Have the Chief Risk Officer read and sign the final report content before submission - their sign-off is the control on cost and root-cause statements.
Submit within one month of the intermediate report, capture the third acknowledgement id and close the notification thread on the incident record.
Attach the submitted final report to the compliance evidence repository under the incident id.
checklist.done: the final report is submitted inside one month, CRO-signed, with the acknowledgement id filed against the incident.

checklist.step: Test the incident against the Solvency II predefined-events list
actions: Open the predefined-events schedule maintained under Solvency II Directive Art. 35(2)(a)(ii) and read the events the NCA expects to be reported outside the routine cycle.
Compare the incident against each listed event - loss of a critical function, material breach of the risk management system, events likely to affect the solvency position - and record the comparison.
Where the incident meets a predefined event, instruct the Regulatory Reporting Manager to send the separate Solvency II notification; a DORA major-incident report does not discharge it.
Log the assessment on the incident record whether or not it triggers, so the not-triggered decision is auditable.
checklist.done: a written predefined-event assessment sits on the incident record and any triggered Solvency II notification has been sent.

checklist.step: Keep the internal model change policy current and approved
actions: Review the Internal Model Change Policy annually against Directive Art. 115 and Delegated Regulation Art. 245 and confirm it still defines minor and major changes, the quantitative triggers and the accumulation rule.

Confirm the quantitative triggers are expressed as a measurable change in SCR (for example a change moving the SCR or a risk module by more than the policy percentage) and that the qualitative triggers cover methodology, scope and data-source changes.
Take the reviewed policy to the AMSB for approval and lodge the approved version, version number and approval date in the model governance repository.
Notify the NCA of any amendment to the change policy itself, since the policy forms part of the approved model.
checklist.done: the current policy version is board-approved, dated, holds measurable minor/major triggers and any amendment has been notified to the NCA.

checklist.step: Classify every model change and route majors for supervisory approval
actions: Open a change record for every proposed internal model change with the requesting function, the risk module touched and the intended first-use valuation date.
Quantify the SCR impact by running the model twice on the same data - before and after the change - and record the delta by module and in total.
Apply the policy triggers to the delta and classify the change minor or major; where a change is borderline, classify up and note why.

For major changes, prepare the application dossier (description, justification, quantitative impact, validation report) and hand it to the Regulatory Reporting Manager, and set the model release gate so the change cannot be used in a reported SCR until approval lands.
Record the NCA decision date and reference on the change record when approval is received.
checklist.done: every change record carries a measured SCR delta, a classification against the policy triggers, and majors are gated pending a recorded NCA approval.

checklist.step: Report accumulated minor changes on the policy cadence
actions: Extract all changes classified minor since the last accumulation report and sum their individual SCR impacts by risk module and in total.

Compare the accumulated impact to the policy threshold at which combined minor changes become a major change; where the threshold is passed, reclassify to major and start the approval route immediately.
Draft the accumulated minor change report listing each change, its date, its module and its impact, plus the combined effect, and have the Model Risk Manager review it.
Hand the report to the Regulatory Reporting Manager for submission to the NCA on the cadence set in the approved change policy.
checklist.done: the accumulation report is produced on cadence, totals reconcile to the change register and any threshold breach has been reclassified as major.

checklist.step: Reflect the approved model position in the S.25 templates
actions: Select the correct template for the model position at the valuation date: S.25.01 for standard formula, S.25.02 for standard formula with partial internal model, S.25.03 for full internal model, following the Annex II instructions of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/2450.
Populate the SCR by risk module from the model run that used only approved model versions - confirm against the change register that no gated major change fed the numbers.
Complete the approach-to-tax-rate and USP flags the template requires and add the narrative on the method used.
Reconcile the template total SCR to the capital calculation pack signed off by the Head of Capital Management before release.
checklist.done: the S.25 template in use matches the approved model status, uses only approved model versions and ties to the signed capital pack.

checklist.step: Retain the incident and model change evidence
actions: Move each closed incident dossier (record export, classification worksheet, three submissions with acknowledgement ids, provider statement, root-cause report) into the compliance evidence repository indexed by incident id and classification date.
Move each model change dossier (change record, SCR delta run, validation report, NCA application and decision) into the same repository indexed by change id and first-use valuation date.
Apply the 10-year retention label and confirm both indexes are searchable by date, NCA acknowledgement id and risk module.
Report the quarter's retained dossier counts to the Compliance Officer against the ITSM and register counts.
checklist.done: every closed incident and model change has a labelled, searchable dossier and the counts agree with the source registers.

testing.step: Build the population of incidents and model changes for the quarter
actions: Extract from ServiceNow every incident with category ICT or Operational and priority P1 or P2 with a detection date inside the quarter, including cancelled and reclassified records.
Extract from the model governance repository every change record with a decision or first-use date inside the quarter.
Add SIEM-originated security incidents and third-party outage notifications so incidents raised outside the service desk cannot be missed.
Sign the population as complete with the record counts and the extract timestamp.
testing.done: a signed, timestamped population of incidents and model changes with the extract counts recorded.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the source of record
actions: Reconcile the ITSM incident count to the SOC's monthly incident summary and to the availability breaches shown in the service-level reporting.
Reconcile the model change count to the version history in the actuarial modelling platform - every model version bump should have a change record behind it.
Investigate and clear every difference before sampling; unexplained differences become population-completeness exceptions in their own right.
testing.done: incident and model change populations reconcile to SOC reporting and model version history with differences cleared or logged.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of incidents classified major and 100% of model changes classified major.
Take 25 not-major incidents by seeded random selection and 10 minor model changes, minimum 40 items in total.
Record the seed, population sizes, selection date and the selection tool in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all major incidents and all major model changes, with the seed recorded.

testing.step: Re-perform the major-incident classification independently
actions: For each sampled incident, re-run the underlying client, transaction, downtime and geography queries against the enterprise data warehouse before reading the classification worksheet.
Reach your own major / not-major conclusion against the classification criteria and only then compare it to the recorded call.
Treat any not-major call that your re-performance makes major as a reportable breach, and any right answer with an unsupported criterion value as an exception.
Capture the query outputs and the GRC worksheet screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled incident has an independent classification conclusion with source query evidence attached.

testing.step: Recompute the 4-hour, 24-hour, 72-hour and one-month clocks
actions: For every major incident, take the awareness and classification timestamps in UTC and recompute initial due = min(classification + 4h, awareness + 24h), intermediate due = initial submission + 72h, final due = intermediate submission + 1 month.
Compare each recomputed deadline to the actual submission timestamp on the NCA acknowledgement, not to the internal record.
Challenge any awareness timestamp that is later than the first SIEM or monitoring alert for the same event and restate the clock where it is.
List every breach in minutes late, with the deadline missed.
testing.done: all four clocks are recomputed from source timestamps and every late submission is quantified in minutes.

testing.step: Trace each notification to an NCA acknowledgement
actions: Open the submission history in the Internal Regulatory System for each sampled major incident and confirm three distinct submissions exist with distinct acknowledgement ids.
Open each submitted form and check the entity LEI, incident reference, affected Member States and impact figures match the classification worksheet.
Where a fallback channel was used, confirm the fallback and reason were logged and that the NCA replied confirming receipt.
Capture the acknowledgement screens into the workpaper.
testing.done: every major incident traces to three acknowledged submissions whose content agrees with the classification worksheet.

testing.step: Test the model change classification and the approval gate
actions: For each sampled model change, re-read the approved Internal Model Change Policy as it stood at the change date and apply its triggers to the recorded SCR delta yourself.
Re-run or inspect the before/after model runs and confirm the recorded delta is reproducible on the same data.
For every major change, confirm a dated NCA approval reference exists and that the first-use valuation date is on or after that approval date.
Treat any major change reflected in a reported SCR before approval as a reportable breach and refer it to the Chief Risk Officer the same day.
testing.done: each sampled change has an independently applied classification and no major change was used in a reported SCR before its approval date.

testing.step: Recompute the accumulated minor change position
actions: Sum the SCR impacts of all minor changes since the last accumulation report, by module and in total, from the change register rather than from the report.
Compare the total to the accumulation threshold in the approved policy and confirm the reported figure matches your recomputation.
Confirm the accumulation report was sent to the NCA on the cadence the policy specifies and that an acknowledgement exists.
Where the threshold was passed without reclassification to major, raise it as a breach.
testing.done: the accumulated minor change total is independently recomputed, agrees to the report and was submitted on cadence.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception carrying the incident or change id, the deadline or trigger missed, the minutes or days late and the supervisory impact.
Assign a root cause (late awareness stamping, classification deferred past the clock, impact data unavailable, third-party silence, change gate bypassed) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and, for missed statutory clocks, open a self-notification assessment with the Regulatory Reporting Manager and Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has a GRC issue with root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the on-time notification rate and the classification agreement rate and compare both to the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each statement.
Have the independent reviewer, who worked none of the sampled incidents and authored no sampled model change classification, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any reportable breaches to the Risk Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, on-time and agreement rates, and a Risk Committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Lock the valuation date data cut
actions: Trigger the capital data extract in the warehouse for the valuation date: in-force policy data, claims and reserve triangles, asset holdings by CIC and NACE code, reinsurance recoverables by counterparty and rating, and deferred tax balances.

Run the agreed data quality suite with the Data Quality Manager - completeness against policy counts, currency and CIC code validity, missing rating and duration fields - and get the pass report before releasing the cut.
Freeze the extract with a run id and record row counts per feed; any post-freeze data change requires a new run id, never an in-place edit.
Reconcile total assets and total technical provisions in the cut to the general ledger balances supplied by the Controller and document the reconciling items.
checklist.done: a frozen, run-id stamped data cut that passes the data quality suite and reconciles to the ledger.

checklist.step: Load the EIOPA risk-free rate term structure and market data
actions: Download the EIOPA monthly risk-free interest rate term structure for the valuation date, in the correct currency set and with and without volatility adjustment as the entity is approved to use.
Confirm the file is the published version for that month, record its publication date, and check the last liquid point and extrapolation parameters are the ones the entity applies.
Pull market inputs from Bloomberg for equity indices, property indices, credit spreads by rating and duration, and FX rates as at the valuation date close.
Load both sets into the actuarial modelling platform and run the load reconciliation report so the curve loaded equals the curve published, point by point.
checklist.done: the published EIOPA curve for the valuation date is loaded and reconciled point-by-point, with market inputs dated to the valuation close.

checklist.step: Take the Solvency II balance sheet and technical provisions handover
actions: Take from the Reserving Actuary the best estimate liability by line of business, gross and net of reinsurance, with the cash-flow projections behind it.
Compute the risk margin using the cost-of-capital method at the prescribed 6% rate applied to the projected SCR of the reference undertaking, and record the projection approach used.
Assemble the Solvency II balance sheet: assets at fair value, technical provisions as BEL plus risk margin, other liabilities, and derive excess of assets over liabilities.
Sign the handover note stating the BEL and risk margin figures being carried into the SCR run and the run id of the data cut they came from.
checklist.done: a signed handover with BEL, risk margin and the Solvency II balance sheet, tied to the frozen data cut run id.

checklist.step: Run the market risk sub-modules
actions: Run interest rate risk on both the up and down shocked curves and take the higher net asset value loss as the sub-module charge.

Run equity risk splitting type 1 and type 2 holdings, applying the symmetric adjustment published for the valuation date, and apply the duration-based or transitional equity treatment only where the entity is approved for it.

Run property, spread (by rating and modified duration, with the qualifying infrastructure and securitisation treatments applied), currency (both directions per currency) and market concentration (single-name exposures against the relative excess threshold by rating).
Aggregate the sub-modules using the market risk correlation matrix, applying the up or down interest-rate correlation set that matches the scenario selected in the first step.
Record each sub-module charge and the driving positions in the module output pack.
checklist.done: all six market sub-modules are run and aggregated with the correlation set matching the selected interest-rate scenario.

checklist.step: Run the counterparty default risk module
actions: Build the type 1 exposure list: reinsurance recoverables by counterparty, cash at bank, derivatives and letters of credit, each with the counterparty credit quality step and the risk-mitigating effect claimed.
Build the type 2 exposure list: intermediary receivables, policyholder debtors past due more than three months, and mortgage loans meeting the criteria.
Take collateral values from the treaty repository and apply the collateral haircut rules before netting them against exposures.
Compute the loss-given-default and the charge for each type, and confirm every counterparty rating used ties to the rating file supplied by the Reinsurance Manager.
checklist.done: type 1 and type 2 exposures are complete, collateral-adjusted and rating-sourced, with the module charge computed.

checklist.step: Run the life, health and non-life underwriting modules
actions: Run the life module sub-risks - mortality, longevity, disability-morbidity, lapse (up, down and mass lapse, taking the highest), expense, revision and life catastrophe - on the BEL cash flows.
Run the health module split into SLT health, NSLT health and health catastrophe, using the prescribed volume measures and standard deviations by segment.

Run the non-life module: premium and reserve risk from earned/written premium and best estimate reserve volume measures by line of business, lapse risk, and catastrophe risk from the CAT Modeler's scenario or standardised output.
Confirm with the Chief Actuary in writing which undertaking-specific parameters are approved and used, and that no unapproved USP has been applied.
Aggregate the sub-risks in each module with the prescribed correlation matrices and record the charges.
checklist.done: life, health and non-life module charges are produced from approved volume measures with only NCA-approved USPs applied.

checklist.step: Aggregate the modules into the Basic SCR
actions: Load the market, counterparty default, life, health and non-life module charges into the aggregation workbook.
Apply the correlation matrix set out in Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 87 and Annex IV to produce the square-root aggregation.
Add the intangible asset risk charge where intangibles are recognised on the Solvency II balance sheet.
Lock the workbook formulas, protect the correlation cells, and have a second capital actuary tick each module input against the module output pack before the total is used.
checklist.done: the BSCR is produced from the prescribed correlation matrix with every module input tied to its output pack and independently ticked.

checklist.step: Compute the operational risk capital charge
actions: Assemble the Art. 204 inputs: earned premiums and technical provisions (excluding risk margin) for life and non-life, split out unit-linked business, and expenses incurred in the last 12 months for unit-linked.
Compute the premium-based and provision-based measures, take the higher, and cap the result at 30% of the BSCR.
Add the unit-linked expense component at the prescribed 25% of annual expenses incurred for unit-linked business.
Show the cap test explicitly in the workbook so a reviewer can see whether the 30% cap bound the result.
checklist.done: SCR_op is computed on the higher of the premium and provision measures, capped at 30% of BSCR, with the unit-linked expense component added and the cap test visible.

checklist.step: Compute the loss-absorbing capacity of technical provisions and deferred taxes
actions: Compute LAC-TP as the reduction in future discretionary benefits under each shock, limited to the value of future discretionary benefits in the BEL and consistent with the entity's approved management actions.
Compute the gross-to-net effect consistently across modules so the adjustment is not double counted between module-level and aggregate-level netting.

Work with the Tax Manager on LAC-DT: quantify the notional deferred tax movement from the instantaneous loss equal to BSCR + SCR_op, and support recoverability with projected future taxable profits, carry-back and reversal of deferred tax liabilities.
Write the LAC-DT recoverability memo naming the evidence relied on, and cap the adjustment where the recoverability evidence does not support it.
checklist.done: LAC-TP and LAC-DT are computed with no double counting and LAC-DT is supported by a signed recoverability memo.

checklist.step: Derive the SCR and the MCR
actions: Compute SCR = BSCR + SCR_op + Adj, where Adj is the combined LAC-TP and LAC-DT adjustment, as required by Art. 103.
Compute the linear MCR from the prescribed factors applied to technical provisions and written premiums by line of business.
Apply the corridor: MCR is the linear MCR floored at 25% and capped at 45% of the SCR, then floored at the absolute minimum capital requirement for the entity's authorised classes.
Show which of the linear, corridor or absolute floor is binding, and record the SCR and MCR coverage ratios against eligible own funds supplied by the Head of Capital Management.
checklist.done: SCR and MCR are derived with the binding MCR constraint identified and coverage ratios computed against eligible own funds.

checklist.step: Confirm the approved simplifications and undertaking-specific parameters
actions: List every simplification applied (for example simplified spread risk, simplified counterparty default, simplified risk margin) and check each against the proportionality conditions in the Delegated Regulation.
Confirm each USP in use has a current NCA approval reference and that the underlying data still meets the approval conditions.
Where a simplification no longer meets its proportionality test, direct the Capital Model Actuary to re-run the module on the full method before sign-off.
Record the approved list, with references and the valuation date it applies from, in the model governance repository.
checklist.done: every simplification passes its proportionality test and every USP carries a current NCA approval reference for the valuation date.

checklist.step: Obtain independent validation of the calculation
actions: Re-perform the aggregation from module outputs to SCR in a separate workbook built independently of the production workbook.
Re-perform two modules in full each quarter on a rotating basis and the operational risk charge every quarter.
Review the manual adjustment log, challenge each entry and require the preparer to evidence any override of model output.
Issue a validation report with findings rated and a clear statement on whether the SCR is fit for reporting.
checklist.done: a validation report exists with an independent aggregation re-performance, rotating module re-performance and a fit-for-reporting statement.

checklist.step: Produce the analysis of change against the prior calculation
actions: Build a module-level bridge from the prior quarter SCR to the current SCR: opening, model/method change, data change, market movement, new business, run-off, reinsurance change, closing.
Explain every module movement above the materiality threshold with a named driver and the position that caused it.
Challenge any module that moved by less than the threshold when the underlying exposure changed materially - a static charge on a moving book usually means a stale input.
Circulate the bridge to the Chief Financial Officer and Chief Risk Officer ahead of sign-off.
checklist.done: a module-level bridge exists where every material movement has a named driver and no material exposure change is left unexplained.

checklist.step: Populate the SCR reporting templates
actions: Populate S.25.01 with the module and total SCR, and the S.26.01 to S.26.07 templates with the sub-module detail for market, counterparty default, life, health, non-life and operational risk, following the Annex II instructions of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/2450.
Populate S.27.01 for non-life catastrophe risk and S.28.01 or S.28.02 for the MCR, depending on whether the entity writes only life, only non-life, or both.
Run the taxonomy validation and clear every blocking error and every non-blocking error with a documented reason.
Tie each populated cell group back to the capital pack line it came from and record the tie-out in the submission file.
checklist.done: S.25, S.26, S.27 and S.28 are populated, validation-clean and tied cell-group by cell-group to the capital pack.

checklist.step: Sign off and file the capital pack
actions: Read the capital pack (SCR by module, MCR with the binding constraint, coverage ratios, analysis of change, validation report and the exceptions log) and challenge the material movements.
Sign the pack, naming the data cut run id, the model versions used and the date, and approve each manual adjustment above the materiality threshold individually.
Release the signed pack to the Regulatory Reporting Manager as the only version permitted to feed the supervisory submission.
File the pack and all supporting runs in the financial reporting repository under the valuation date with a 10-year retention label.
checklist.done: a CFO-signed capital pack naming the run id and model versions is filed and is the sole source for the supervisory submission.

testing.step: Build the population of capital calculation runs
actions: List every SCR and MCR calculation run in the period by entity and valuation date, including re-runs and abandoned runs, from the model run log.
Add the group calculation runs and confirm each solo entity in the group scope appears.
Confirm which run id fed each supervisory submission and flag any submission fed by a run other than the signed one.
testing.done: a complete run inventory by entity and valuation date, with the submission-feeding run identified for each.

testing.step: Reconcile calculation inputs to the source of record
actions: Reconcile total assets, technical provisions and other liabilities in the Solvency II balance sheet to the general ledger and the statutory accounts, and agree the Solvency II valuation adjustments line by line.
Reconcile the asset holdings by CIC code used in market risk to the custodian position report and to Aladdin.
Reconcile reinsurance recoverables used in counterparty default to the ceded accounting platform.
Investigate every difference above the materiality threshold before sampling.
testing.done: balance sheet, asset and recoverable inputs reconcile to ledger, custodian and ceded records with differences cleared.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of modules and positions
actions: Take 100% of the modules contributing more than 10% of the BSCR and 100% of the operational risk and adjustment calculations.
Take 25 positions by seeded random selection from the market and counterparty exposure lists, weighted to the largest single-name exposures.
Record the seed, population sizes and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all major modules, the adjustments and 25 weighted positions.

testing.step: Re-perform the module calculations independently
actions: Rebuild the sampled module charges from the frozen data cut in an independent workbook, applying the shocks straight from the Delegated Regulation rather than from the production configuration.

For interest rate risk, confirm the up and down shocked curves were both run and the higher loss taken; for equity risk, confirm the symmetric adjustment used is the value published for the valuation date.
For spread and concentration risk, re-derive the credit quality step and duration for the sampled positions from the source rating and holding data.
Compare to the production charge and treat any difference above 0.5% of the module charge as an exception with a written cause.
testing.done: each sampled module is independently rebuilt and agrees to production within 0.5%, or the difference is explained and logged.

testing.step: Recompute the BSCR aggregation and the operational risk charge
actions: Rebuild the square-root aggregation from the module charges using the Art. 87 and Annex IV correlation matrix typed in from the regulation text, not copied from the production workbook.
Confirm the interest-rate correlation set used matches the up or down scenario that was selected as binding.
Recompute SCR_op from earned premiums, technical provisions and unit-linked expenses, apply the 30% BSCR cap and confirm which limb bound.
Recompute SCR = BSCR + SCR_op + Adj and compare to the reported SCR.
testing.done: BSCR, SCR_op and total SCR are independently recomputed and agree to the reported SCR within 0.5%.

testing.step: Test the LAC-TP and LAC-DT adjustments
actions: Confirm the LAC-TP adjustment does not exceed the value of future discretionary benefits in the BEL and that the management actions assumed match those in the approved management actions policy.
Recompute the notional deferred tax movement from an instantaneous loss equal to BSCR + SCR_op at the enacted tax rate.

Read the LAC-DT recoverability memo and test the projected future taxable profits against the board-approved business plan; treat unsupported recoverability as an exception requiring the adjustment to be capped.
Confirm the gross-to-net treatment is applied once and not both at module and aggregate level.
testing.done: both adjustments are recomputed, bounded by their regulatory limits and supported by plan-based recoverability evidence.

testing.step: Recompute the MCR corridor and identify the binding constraint
actions: Recompute the linear MCR from the prescribed factors and the technical provisions and written premiums by line of business.
Apply the 25% and 45% of SCR corridor and the absolute minimum capital requirement for the entity's authorised classes.
Confirm the reported MCR is the correct binding value and that the reported figure matches template S.28.
Recompute the SCR and MCR coverage ratios from eligible own funds and compare to the reported ratios.
testing.done: the MCR is recomputed with the correct binding constraint and both coverage ratios agree to the reported figures.

testing.step: Test the manual adjustments and simplifications
actions: Pull the manual adjustment log for the sampled runs and test each entry for a documented rationale, a supporting calculation and CFO approval where it exceeds the materiality threshold.
For each simplification applied, re-perform the proportionality test against the conditions in the Delegated Regulation on the current book.
Confirm every USP used carries a live NCA approval reference covering the valuation date.
Treat any adjustment overriding model output without evidence, and any simplification failing its proportionality test, as a fail.
testing.done: every manual adjustment is evidenced and approved, and every simplification and USP passes its test with a live approval reference.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception with the entity, valuation date, module, the quantified capital effect and whether the reported SCR is misstated.
Assign a root cause (stale market data, wrong correlation set, unapproved simplification, data quality failure, unevidenced override) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where a reported solvency ratio is misstated, open a resubmission assessment with the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's validation as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception carries a quantified capital effect, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the validation
actions: Compute the aggregate difference between recomputed and reported SCR as a percentage and compare it to the 0.5% threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who neither built nor ran the tested models, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any misstatement to the Audit Committee and the Risk Committee at their next sittings and file the workpaper in the model governance repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, the recomputation variance and committee reporting dates exists in the repository.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Solvency II Directive 2009/138/EC Art. 44 (risk management system) with Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 259(1) (AMSB responsibility for the risk management system), and Arts. 138(2) and 142 (SCR non-compliance, recovery plan, deteriorating financial conditions), re-read at each annual limit review

In-scope processes.value: Board risk-appetite setting, translation into solvency intervention levels, daily/weekly solvency monitoring and roll-forward, limit breach escalation, supervisory notification and recovery or finance scheme production

In-scope systems.value: Limits, breach records and escalation workflow live in the GRC platform; the solvency dashboard is published in Power BI from the capital roll-forward, with asset triggers monitored in BlackRock Aladdin

Compliance procedure documented.value: Capital Monitoring and Escalation Procedure - the intervention ladder, roll-forward method, breach definitions, escalation routes and timings, and the Art. 138/139 notification and recovery plan steps

Compliance procedure approved.value: Risk appetite statement and intervention ladder approved by the AMSB annually; the escalation procedure approved by the Chief Risk Officer and reviewed after every amber or red event

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: SCR breach: notify the supervisor immediately, submit a realistic recovery plan within 2 months of observing the breach and restore within 6 months (extendable by 3 months); MCR breach: notify immediately, submit a short-term realistic finance scheme within 1 month and restore within 3 months; deteriorating financial conditions under Art. 138(4)/142 notified as they arise

Deadline reminders configured.value: GRC breach records auto-set the notification task at breach date +0 days, the recovery plan task at +45 days and the restoration checkpoint at +5 months for SCR; +20 days and +2 months for MCR, with the CFO on every alert

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Dated solvency dashboards, roll-forward workings, limit breach records with disposition, board and risk committee minutes and any supervisory notifications retained 10 years in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every amber and red ladder trigger is a GRC breach record with the trigger value, the date observed, escalation timestamps, management action taken and the closure decision by the CRO

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs the closure of every limit breach and confirms the ratio returned above the trigger before the record is closed

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every daily and weekly solvency monitoring observation in the period, every ladder trigger event recorded, and every escalation, notification and recovery action taken

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on unescalated triggers - any observation below a trigger without a GRC breach record inside the procedure's escalation window is a fail; any SCR or MCR breach not notified to the supervisor immediately is a reportable breach

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous; the test runs quarterly over the full period of observations with 100% coverage of amber and red events and a sample of green observations to prove the calculation

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside Capital Management and Finance and must not have produced any tested dashboard

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly capital monitoring test workpaper (observation extract, roll-forward recomputation, breach trace, escalation timing analysis) in the compliance evidence repository

checklist.step: Take the board-approved risk appetite and tolerance limits
actions: Table the risk appetite statement at the AMSB annually with the proposed solvency appetite expressed as an SCR coverage range and a hard floor.
Have the board approve the appetite, the tolerance limits per material risk category and the escalation authority at each level, and record the approval in the minutes on the board portal.
Capture from the minutes the exact approved numbers and the effective date so the ladder can be calibrated to them rather than to an interpretation.
Hand the approved statement to the Capital Management Manager and the Enterprise Risk Manager for translation into monitoring triggers.
checklist.done: a minuted, dated board approval of the solvency appetite range, hard floor and per-risk tolerance limits.

checklist.step: Calibrate the solvency intervention ladder
actions: Translate the board appetite into named ladder levels with numeric SCR coverage triggers - for example green above the appetite range, amber inside a management-action zone, red approaching the regulatory floor, and breach below 100% SCR coverage.
Set the equivalent MCR ladder, remembering MCR coverage below 100% carries the shortest statutory clock.
Attach to each level the required action, the accountable role and the escalation deadline in working days or hours.
Configure the levels as limit records in the GRC platform so an observation below a trigger automatically opens a breach record rather than relying on someone raising it.
checklist.done: a numeric ladder for SCR and MCR coverage is configured in GRC with an owner, action and escalation clock at each level.

checklist.step: Build the solvency monitoring dashboard
actions: Build a dashboard showing SCR coverage, MCR coverage, eligible own funds by tier and the distance to each ladder trigger, refreshed on the agreed daily or weekly cadence.
Source own funds from the last signed capital pack and movements from the ledger and the investment position feed so the roll-forward is auditable to two sources.
Show the observation date, the data as-at date and the last full calculation date on the face of the dashboard so a stale roll-forward is visible.
Distribute to the CFO, CRO, Head of Capital Management and the Risk Committee secretary on a fixed schedule and archive each dated version.
checklist.done: a dated dashboard publishes on cadence showing both coverage ratios, tier composition, distance to trigger and the as-at dates.

checklist.step: Run the solvency roll-forward between full calculations
actions: Roll the last full SCR forward using the agreed sensitivities: interest rate and credit spread moves, equity and property index moves, FX, new business volumes and the period's claims experience.
Roll own funds forward for the period result, dividends declared or foreseeable, unrealised gains and losses and any capital instrument movement notified by the Treasury Manager.

Compare the roll-forward result to the last full calculation at the last common date and record the tracking error; where the error exceeds the tolerance in the procedure, trigger an early full recalculation.
Publish the roll-forward inputs and outputs alongside the dashboard so the ratio can be reconstructed.
checklist.done: each published ratio has a documented roll-forward with its inputs, and the tracking error against the last full run is inside tolerance.

checklist.step: Monitor the MCR corridor position separately
actions: Recompute the MCR each monitoring cycle, since a falling SCR pulls the 25% floor and 45% cap of the corridor with it and can move the MCR independently of the linear result.
Track eligible own funds for MCR coverage separately - Tier 3 and ancillary own funds do not count toward the MCR, so MCR coverage can breach while SCR coverage looks adequate.
Flag on the dashboard which limb of the corridor is binding and how far the entity is from the absolute minimum capital requirement floor.
Alert the CFO immediately whenever MCR coverage falls below the amber trigger, ahead of the routine cycle.
checklist.done: MCR coverage is monitored on its own eligible own funds basis each cycle with the binding corridor limb shown.

checklist.step: Monitor the market and ALM triggers that move the ratio fastest
actions: Set alerts in Aladdin on the market variables the sensitivity analysis shows move coverage most: parallel rate shifts, credit spread widening by rating band, equity index falls and the symmetric adjustment level.
Set duration and convexity mismatch limits between assets and the liability cash flows and alert when the mismatch exceeds the ALM policy tolerance.
Report to the Capital Management Manager the same day any alert fires, with the estimated coverage effect using the published sensitivities.
Escalate concentration or downgrade events on single counterparties to the Reinsurance Credit and Security Analyst for the counterparty default impact.
checklist.done: market and ALM alerts are configured to the published sensitivities and fire same-day to Capital Management with an estimated coverage effect.

checklist.step: Escalate amber triggers to the Risk Committee
actions: Open the auto-raised GRC breach record and complete it within the escalation window: trigger level, observed ratio, observation date, driver analysis and the roll-forward reference.
Convene the escalation call named in the ladder with the CFO, CRO and Head of Capital Management inside the working-day deadline for that level.
Record the management actions selected, their owners and their expected coverage effect on the record.
Report the event and the actions to the Risk Committee at its next sitting and add it to the standing breach report.
checklist.done: each amber trigger has a completed breach record, a timed escalation call and named management actions with owners.

checklist.step: Notify the supervisor immediately on an SCR breach or risk of breach
actions: Where SCR coverage falls below 100%, or where the entity observes that it is at risk of doing so in the following three months, inform the supervisory authority immediately - the trigger is observation, not confirmation by a full recalculation.
Draft the notification with the observed ratio, the observation date, the drivers, the immediate actions taken and the expected trajectory, and have Regulatory Counsel clear the wording.
Send it through the supervisory reporting channel, capture the acknowledgement and the receiving supervisor's name, and log both on the GRC breach record.
Brief the AMSB chair the same day and put the breach on the next board agenda as a standing item until closed.
checklist.done: the supervisor is notified on the observation date with an acknowledgement logged and the board chair briefed same-day.

checklist.step: Produce the realistic recovery plan within two months
actions: Build the recovery plan showing how eligible own funds covering the SCR, or the risk profile, will be restored within six months of the observation date.

Quantify each measure - capital injection, reinsurance purchase, de-risking of the asset portfolio, dividend suspension, new business restriction - with its coverage effect, its execution date and its owner and its dependency (for example shareholder approval).
Show the projected quarterly coverage path to restoration and state the assumptions the path relies on, so the supervisor can test them.
Have the AMSB approve the plan, then submit it within two months of the observation date and record the acknowledgement.
checklist.done: a board-approved recovery plan with quantified, dated, owned measures and a projected coverage path is submitted inside two months.

checklist.step: Run the MCR breach route on its shorter clock
actions: On observing MCR coverage below 100%, notify the supervisor immediately and mark the breach record MCR so the one-month clock, not the two-month clock, is applied.
Prepare the short-term realistic finance scheme showing restoration of eligible basic own funds to at least the MCR, or reduction of the risk profile, within three months of observation.
Restrict to basic own funds items eligible for MCR coverage when quantifying the measures - ancillary own funds and Tier 3 do not count.
Obtain AMSB approval and submit within one month of observation, then report progress to the supervisor monthly until closure.
checklist.done: the MCR notification is immediate and a board-approved finance scheme using MCR-eligible own funds is submitted inside one month.

checklist.step: Keep the management action playbook executable
actions: Maintain a playbook listing each available capital action with its realistic coverage effect, execution lead time, cost and the approvals it needs.

Refresh the lead times quarterly with the Chief Investment Officer and the Head of Reinsurance - a de-risking trade or a quota share that takes longer than the recovery window is not a recovery measure.
Pre-clear with Regulatory Counsel which measures need supervisory approval or notification, such as own-funds item redemptions.
Test one measure a year end-to-end on paper with the Risk Committee to prove it could actually be executed.
checklist.done: the playbook shows a current lead time, coverage effect and approval path for every measure and one measure is tested annually.

checklist.step: Assess deteriorating financial conditions beyond the ratio
actions: Each cycle, review the non-ratio indicators the supervisor may treat as deteriorating financial conditions: adverse claims development, liquidity strain, ratings actions, loss of a major reinsurance panel member or a material operational loss.
Where indicators point to deterioration even with adequate coverage, record the assessment and consider a voluntary supervisory notification under Arts. 138(4) and 142.
Link the assessment to the ORSA so the forward-looking view and the monitoring view do not diverge.
Table the assessment at the Risk Committee with a recommendation.
checklist.done: a documented deteriorating-conditions assessment exists each cycle with a Risk Committee recommendation and an ORSA linkage.

checklist.step: Maintain the breach register and dispositions
actions: Keep one register row per trigger event with observation date, level, ratio, driver, escalation timestamps, actions, supervisory notification reference and closure date.
Require the ratio to be back above the trigger for two consecutive monitoring cycles before a record can move to closed.
Have the Chief Risk Officer sign each closure and record the signature and date on the row.
Publish the open and closed counts in the monthly risk report.
checklist.done: every trigger event has a register row with escalation timestamps and a CRO-signed closure supported by two clear cycles.

checklist.step: Report the position to the board every cycle
actions: Include in every board and Risk Committee pack the current SCR and MCR coverage, the distance to each ladder trigger, the trend since the last meeting and the open breach records.
Minute the board's challenge and any decision to change appetite, restrict dividends or restrict new business, with the decision date.
Confirm the AMSB has discharged its Art. 259(1) responsibility by evidencing the discussion, not merely the tabling of the pack.
Circulate the approved minutes to the CFO and CRO for action tracking.
checklist.done: each board and Risk Committee pack shows both ratios and open breaches, and the minutes evidence board challenge and decisions.

checklist.step: Retain the monitoring evidence
actions: Archive every dated dashboard, its roll-forward workings and its source extracts into the compliance evidence repository indexed by observation date and entity.
Archive each closed breach record with its escalation timestamps, supervisory notifications, recovery plan and board minutes.
Apply the 10-year retention label and confirm the archive is searchable by observation date, ladder level and entity.
Reconcile the archived dashboard count to the expected count for the cadence and chase any missing cycle.
checklist.done: every monitoring cycle and breach record is archived, labelled and searchable, with no missing cycles in the series.

testing.step: Build the population of monitoring observations and trigger events
actions: Extract every published solvency dashboard in the period with its observation date, SCR coverage, MCR coverage and ladder level.
Extract every GRC breach record raised in the period, including records raised and later withdrawn.
Count the published dashboards against the expected count for the cadence and list every missing cycle as a completeness exception before going further.
testing.done: a dated observation series with no unexplained gaps and a full list of trigger events, signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the observations to the signed capital packs
actions: Agree each quarter's opening roll-forward position to the CFO-signed capital pack for that valuation date.
Agree own funds movements in the roll-forward to the general ledger result, declared dividends and the Treasury Manager's capital instrument log.
Recompute the tracking error between the final roll-forward before each full calculation and the full calculation result, and test it against the procedure tolerance.
testing.done: roll-forwards tie to signed capital packs and ledger movements, and every tracking error is inside the procedure tolerance or explained.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of amber, red and breach observations and 100% of the associated GRC records.
Take 20 green observations by seeded random selection spread across the period to test the calculation and publication controls.
Record the seed, the population size and the selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering every non-green observation and 20 green observations across the period.

testing.step: Re-perform the ladder classification on the sample
actions: Read the board-approved appetite statement in force at each sampled observation date and the ladder configuration as it stood then.
Recompute the coverage ratios from the roll-forward inputs and classify the observation against the ladder yourself before reading the recorded level.
Treat any observation classified green that your recomputation puts amber or worse as an exception, and any ladder configuration that does not match the board-approved numbers as a control failure.
Capture the GRC limit configuration screen and the board appetite extract into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled observation has an independently recomputed ratio and ladder classification tied to the appetite in force on that date.

testing.step: Test escalation timeliness against the procedure clocks
actions: For every trigger event, take the observation timestamp and the GRC record creation, escalation call and action-decision timestamps.
Recompute the elapsed time against the escalation window the ladder sets for that level and record any breach in working hours.
Check the escalation reached the roles the ladder names - an amber escalated only within Capital Management when the ladder requires the CFO is a fail.
Confirm each event appeared in the next Risk Committee pack after it was raised.
testing.done: every trigger event has a measured escalation elapsed time against its required window and a traced committee reporting date.

testing.step: Trace SCR and MCR breaches to immediate supervisory notification
actions: For every observation below 100% SCR or MCR coverage, find the supervisory notification in the Internal Regulatory System and read its submission timestamp.
Compare it to the observation date - immediate means the same business day, so any gap requires a written explanation and is presumed a breach.
Confirm the notification content states the observed ratio, date and drivers and was cleared by Regulatory Counsel.
Confirm the board chair briefing and board agenda entry exist for the same date.
testing.done: every coverage breach traces to a same-day, counsel-cleared supervisory notification with an acknowledgement and a board briefing.

testing.step: Recompute the recovery plan and finance scheme deadlines
actions: For each SCR breach, recompute the recovery plan due date as observation date plus two months and the restoration checkpoint as observation date plus six months.
For each MCR breach, recompute the finance scheme due date as observation date plus one month and restoration as plus three months.
Compare each recomputed date to the actual submission date on the supervisory acknowledgement and quantify any lateness in days.
Test whether the measures in the plan were executed by their stated dates and whether the projected coverage path was met.
testing.done: all recovery and finance scheme clocks are recomputed from the observation date, with lateness quantified and measure execution tested.

testing.step: Test the eligibility basis used for MCR coverage
actions: Take the own funds items counted toward MCR coverage in the sampled observations and confirm Tier 3 and ancillary own funds were excluded.
Recompute MCR coverage on the correct eligible basis and compare to the reported figure.
Confirm the MCR itself was recomputed each cycle rather than held static, since the 25%/45% corridor moves with the SCR.
Treat any observation where a corrected basis would have crossed a ladder trigger as a reportable exception.
testing.done: MCR coverage is recomputed on the correct eligible own funds basis for every sampled observation with any trigger crossing reported.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception with the observation date, the ladder level involved, the hours or days of delay and whether a statutory clock was missed.
Assign a root cause (stale roll-forward, mis-set limit configuration, escalation not routed to the named role, ineligible own funds counted, notification delayed for internal review) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where a supervisory notification was late, open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel and the CFO.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has a GRC issue with root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the escalation on-time rate and the ladder classification agreement rate and compare both to the zero-tolerance threshold for unescalated triggers.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside Capital Management and Finance and produced none of the tested dashboards, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any missed statutory notification to the Audit Committee and the board and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, escalation and classification rates, and board reporting dates exists in the repository.
