Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Late submissions, resubmissions, unresolved non-blocking validation errors, tier limit breaches and any restatement of a published ratio are logged as filing issues with root cause and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs the submission release and every resubmission or restatement of a previously reported solvency ratio

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every quarterly and annual QRT submission, the SFCR and RSR, for every solo entity and the group, with their validation logs, acknowledgements and the own funds items reported in each

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on missed statutory submission dates and on blocking validation errors at submission; any tier limit breach reported as compliant, or any eligible own funds figure not tying to the tiering test, is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is quarterly and annual; the test runs after each submission cycle with full re-performance of the tiering test annually and a targeted re-performance quarterly

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside the regulatory reporting production team and must not have prepared or submitted the tested filings

Evidence location for test results.value: Post-submission review workpaper (deadline recomputation, tiering re-performance, template-to-ledger reconciliation, validation log review, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Submitted instance documents with acknowledgement ids, the validation logs, the tiering test workbook, the reconciliation to statutory accounts and the board-approved SFCR - producible for an NCA reporting review within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Regulatory Reporting Manager answers NCA data queries and manages resubmissions; the Chief Financial Officer approves any correction to a previously reported solvency or MCR coverage ratio before it is communicated

checklist.step: Build the reporting calendar for the cycle
actions: List every reporting entity and the group, and against each set the statutory submission dates: quarterly solo at 5 weeks after quarter-end, annual solo and SFCR at 14 weeks after year-end, group at 11 and 20 weeks.
Add the NCA's national add-ons and any entity-specific waivers or exemptions from quarterly reporting, quoting the decision reference granting them.
Back off internal milestones from each submission date: data cut, signed capital pack at T-10 working days, validation run at T-7, board approval for the SFCR at T-5.
Publish the calendar to Finance, Actuarial, Risk and the Corporate Secretary and load the milestones as tasks with T-30/T-14/T-5 alerts.
checklist.done: every entity has statutory dates, internal milestones and alerts loaded, with any exemption evidenced by an NCA decision reference.

checklist.step: Classify every own funds item into tiers
actions: List every basic own funds item - ordinary share capital and related share premium, the reconciliation reserve, subordinated liabilities, preference shares, subordinated mutual member accounts and net deferred tax assets - and every ancillary own funds item approved by the NCA.
Classify each item by testing it against the permanent availability and subordination features and the loss-absorbency criteria, not by carrying forward last period's classification.

For each subordinated instrument, read the terms in the contract lifecycle management repository and confirm the maturity, call dates, coupon cancellation and write-down features support the tier claimed.
Record grandfathered instruments separately with their transitional expiry date, since transitional treatment falls away and reclassifies the item.
Confirm net deferred tax assets are classified Tier 3 and that ancillary own funds carry a live NCA approval amount.
checklist.done: every own funds item has a tier with the tested features and, for instruments, the contract terms behind the classification recorded.

checklist.step: Run the quantitative tier limit test
actions: For SCR coverage, test that eligible Tier 1 is at least 50% of the SCR, that Tier 3 is no more than 15% of the SCR, and that restricted Tier 1 items do not exceed 20% of total Tier 1.
For MCR coverage, test that eligible Tier 1 is at least 80% of the MCR, that Tier 2 basic own funds cover no more than 20%, and that Tier 3 and all ancillary own funds are excluded entirely.
Where a limit binds, disallow the excess and carry only the eligible amount into the coverage ratio - never report the full available amount.
Show each limit test as a separate line with the available amount, the limit, the eligible amount and the disallowed excess so a reviewer can see the binding constraint.
checklist.done: each SCR and MCR tier limit is tested on its own line with available, limit, eligible and disallowed amounts shown.

checklist.step: Deduct foreseeable dividends, distributions and charges
actions: Take from the board minutes and the dividend policy any dividend declared or foreseeable at the valuation date, including a proposed dividend not yet approved where it is foreseeable.
Deduct the foreseeable dividends, distributions and charges from the reconciliation reserve before the tiering test runs, not after.
Reconcile the reconciliation reserve to excess of assets over liabilities less own shares, less foreseeable dividends, less other basic own funds items and less restricted ring-fenced fund items.
Have the Chief Financial Officer confirm the foreseeable dividend figure in writing before it is locked.
checklist.done: the reconciliation reserve reconciles to the balance sheet with a CFO-confirmed foreseeable dividend deduction applied before tiering.

checklist.step: Assemble the quantitative reporting templates
actions: Load the template set required for the cycle: S.01 content and basic information, S.02 balance sheet, S.05 premiums claims and expenses, S.06/S.08 assets and derivatives, S.12/S.17 technical provisions, S.19 non-life claims development, S.22 long-term guarantee measures, S.23 own funds, S.25-S.28 capital requirements.
Map each template cell group to its source: the signed capital pack, the Solvency II balance sheet, the asset data extract or the ledger, and record the mapping in the submission file.
Apply the correct reporting currency, entity LEI, reporting reference date and the accounting standard flag on S.01.
Complete the quarterly subset only where a quarterly waiver does not apply, and evidence any waiver with its NCA reference.
checklist.done: the correct template set for the entity and cycle is populated with every cell group mapped to a named source.

checklist.step: Run the taxonomy validation and clear the errors
actions: Generate the XBRL instance against the EIOPA taxonomy version the NCA has mandated for the reference date and confirm the taxonomy version on the instance header.
Run the full validation and export the log; resolve every blocking error at source in the underlying data rather than by overwriting the cell.
For each non-blocking error, write the explanation that will accompany the filing and have the Regulatory Reporting Manager approve it - unexplained non-blocking errors are the most common NCA query.
Re-run the validation until the log shows zero blocking errors and archive the final log with the instance.
checklist.done: the instance validates against the mandated taxonomy with zero blocking errors and every non-blocking error carries an approved explanation.

checklist.step: Reconcile the templates to the ledger and statutory accounts
actions: Reconcile S.02 balance sheet assets and liabilities to the statutory or IFRS balance sheet, listing each Solvency II valuation adjustment with its amount and basis.
Reconcile S.05 premiums, claims and expenses to the income statement by line of business and explain the mapping of statutory lines to Solvency II lines of business.
Reconcile S.23 own funds to the equity statement and to the tiering test workbook, and reconcile S.25 and S.28 to the CFO-signed capital pack.
Sign the reconciliation pack and attach it to the submission file - an unreconciled template is not released.
checklist.done: a signed reconciliation pack ties the balance sheet, income, own funds and capital templates to the ledger and the signed capital pack.

checklist.step: Draft the SFCR narrative
actions: Draft to the prescribed structure: A business and performance, B system of governance, C risk profile, D valuation for solvency purposes, E capital management, following the Annex XX headings of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35.
In section E, describe the own funds structure, the tiering, the material terms of each own funds item, the eligible amounts against SCR and MCR, and explain any tier limit that bound.
Explain each material change from the prior year in own funds, SCR and coverage, and quantify it.
Collect section owners' written confirmations - governance from the Corporate Secretary, risk profile from the CRO, valuation from the Chief Actuary - before the draft goes to the board.
checklist.done: a complete SFCR draft to the Annex XX structure with section-owner confirmations and a quantified explanation of every material movement.

checklist.step: Obtain the required audit or review of the SFCR
actions: Confirm with the Chief Financial Officer which SFCR elements the NCA requires to be audited in the jurisdiction - typically the Solvency II balance sheet and parts of own funds, with technical provisions often carved out.
Provide the external auditor with the reconciliation pack, the tiering test workbook and the signed capital pack, and track their requests to closure in AuditBoard.
Resolve every audit finding before board approval and record the adjustment in the templates, re-running validation after any change.
File the auditor's report or opinion with the SFCR submission package.
checklist.done: the audit scope required by the NCA is completed, findings are cleared into the templates, and the opinion is in the submission package.

checklist.step: Obtain board approval of the SFCR
actions: Table the final SFCR, the reconciliation pack, the validation log summary and the auditor's opinion at the AMSB at least 5 working days before the submission date.
Record the board's approval of the SFCR and of the solvency and MCR coverage ratios it discloses, with the date, in the minutes.
Capture the board's challenge on material movements in the minutes - approval without recorded challenge is a governance finding at the next NCA review.
Release the approved version number to the Regulatory Reporting Manager as the only version permitted for submission and publication.
checklist.done: a minuted AMSB approval of a named SFCR version, with recorded challenge, dated ahead of the submission date.

checklist.step: Submit to the supervisory authority
actions: Submit the validated XBRL instance and the SFCR through the NCA's reporting channel, selecting the correct reporting reference date, entity LEI and submission type (initial or resubmission).
Confirm the submission timestamp is inside the statutory window and capture the acknowledgement id and any receipt-level validation feedback from the NCA.
Where the NCA returns errors on receipt, correct and resubmit inside the same statutory window where possible, and notify the supervisor in writing where it is not.
Log the acknowledgement id, submission timestamp and any feedback against the calendar entry.
checklist.done: each submission carries an NCA acknowledgement id and a timestamp inside its statutory window, with any receipt feedback logged.

checklist.step: Publish the SFCR
actions: Publish the board-approved SFCR on the company website within the same statutory deadline as the submission and keep it accessible for at least five years.
Confirm the published PDF is the board-approved version number and that the disclosed SCR and MCR coverage ratios match the submitted S.23 and S.28.
Where a prior year SFCR is superseded or corrected, publish the corrected version with a clear statement of what changed and the date.
Record the publication URL and date on the calendar entry as the evidence of disclosure.
checklist.done: the approved SFCR is publicly accessible by the deadline, matches the submitted templates, and the URL and date are logged.

checklist.step: Manage resubmissions under the re-filing policy
actions: Assess every post-submission error against the re-filing materiality thresholds the NCA applies and record the assessment even where no re-filing is required.
Where a re-filing is required, raise a tracker issue, correct the source data, re-run validation and resubmit marking the submission type as a resubmission for the same reference date.
Notify the NCA contact in writing of what changed, the reference date affected and the effect on the reported ratios, cleared by the Chief Financial Officer.
Link the resubmission acknowledgement to the original submission record so the filing history is complete.
checklist.done: every post-submission error has a documented materiality assessment and any resubmission is CFO-cleared and linked to the original filing.

checklist.step: Log acknowledgements and close the cycle
actions: Confirm every entity and every template set due in the cycle has an acknowledgement id and mark the calendar entry complete only against that evidence.
List any submission made after its statutory date with the days late and open a filing issue with a root cause.
Report the cycle's completion status, late filings and open validation explanations to the Audit Committee.
Hand the cycle file to the Statutory Reporting Manager for the post-submission review.
checklist.done: every due submission is closed against an acknowledgement id and every late filing has an issue with a root cause.

checklist.step: Retain the filing evidence
actions: Archive per entity and reference date: the submitted instance document, the validation log, the reconciliation pack, the tiering test workbook, the board minutes, the auditor's opinion, the published SFCR and the NCA acknowledgement.
Apply the 10-year retention label and confirm the archive is searchable by entity, reference date and acknowledgement id.
Confirm the published SFCR remains accessible for the required five-year public availability period.
Reconcile the archived submission count to the calendar entries for the cycle.
checklist.done: every submission has a complete labelled archive, searchable by entity and reference date, reconciled to the reporting calendar.

testing.step: Build the population of filings due and made
actions: Derive the population of filings due from the entity list and the statutory frequencies, independently of the reporting calendar, so an entity missing from the calendar cannot hide.
Extract every submission made in the period with entity, reference date, submission type and acknowledgement id.
Match due to made and list every gap and every unexpected extra submission before sampling.
testing.done: an independently derived due list is matched to actual submissions with all gaps and extras listed.

testing.step: Reconcile submitted templates to the source of record
actions: Take the submitted instance documents and agree S.02 to the statutory balance sheet, S.23 to the equity statement and the tiering workbook, and S.25/S.28 to the CFO-signed capital pack.
Confirm the capital pack used was the signed version and not a later or draft run.
Investigate every difference and confirm each Solvency II valuation adjustment in the reconciliation has a stated basis.
testing.done: submitted templates reconcile to statutory accounts and the signed capital pack, with every valuation adjustment based.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of annual submissions and the SFCR for every entity, and 100% of resubmissions.
Take 20 own funds items by seeded random selection, forced to include every subordinated instrument, every grandfathered item and every ancillary own funds item.
Record the seed, population sizes and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all annual filings, all resubmissions and every non-ordinary own funds item.

testing.step: Re-perform the own funds classification on the sample
actions: Pull the instrument documentation for each sampled item and read the maturity, call, coupon cancellation, write-down and subordination terms yourself.
Test the terms against the tier criteria in Delegated Regulation Arts. 69-79 before reading the recorded tier, and reach your own classification.
Confirm grandfathered items are still inside their transitional window at the reference date, and that expired transitionals were reclassified.
Confirm net deferred tax assets sit in Tier 3 and that ancillary own funds do not exceed the NCA-approved amount.
testing.done: each sampled item has an independently derived tier from source contract terms, with transitional expiry and approval limits checked.

testing.step: Recompute the tier limit and eligibility maths
actions: Recompute SCR eligibility: Tier 1 at least 50% of SCR, Tier 3 no more than 15% of SCR, restricted Tier 1 no more than 20% of total Tier 1, and recompute the disallowed excess where a limit binds.
Recompute MCR eligibility: Tier 1 at least 80% of MCR, Tier 2 no more than 20%, Tier 3 and ancillary own funds excluded.
Recompute both coverage ratios from the eligible amounts and compare to the ratios reported in S.23, S.28 and the published SFCR.
Treat any reported ratio built on available rather than eligible own funds as a fail and quantify the overstatement.
testing.done: all tier limits and both coverage ratios are independently recomputed and agree to the reported and published figures.

testing.step: Recompute the submission deadlines and test timeliness
actions: Recompute each due date from the reference date: solo quarterly at 5 weeks, solo annual and SFCR at 14 weeks, group at 11 and 20 weeks.
Compare each recomputed date to the submission timestamp on the NCA acknowledgement, not to the internal calendar completion flag.
Test any claimed exemption or waiver from quarterly reporting against the NCA decision granting it and its validity at the reference date.
Quantify every late submission in days and identify whether an extension was formally granted.
testing.done: every deadline is recomputed from the reference date, timeliness is measured against the acknowledgement, and waivers are evidenced.

testing.step: Review the validation logs and non-blocking explanations
actions: Open the archived validation log for each sampled submission and confirm zero blocking errors at the point of submission.
Read each non-blocking error explanation and test whether it is a genuine reason or a restatement of the error text.
Confirm the taxonomy version on the instance is the one the NCA mandated for that reference date.
Check that any correction made to clear an error was made in the source data and flowed to the reconciliation, not typed over the cell.
testing.done: each submission has a clean blocking-error log, mandated taxonomy version and substantive explanations for non-blocking errors.

testing.step: Trace the SFCR to board approval and public disclosure
actions: Find the AMSB minute approving the SFCR, confirm it names the version submitted and that its date precedes the submission date.
Open the published SFCR at the recorded URL and compare the disclosed SCR and MCR coverage ratios and own funds tiering to the submitted S.23 and S.28.
Confirm the publication date is inside the statutory deadline and that prior-year reports remain accessible for the required period.
Confirm the auditor's opinion covering the NCA-required scope is included with the published and submitted report.
testing.done: the published SFCR matches the board-approved and submitted version, was published on time and carries the required audit opinion.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a filing issue per exception with the entity, reference date, template or SFCR section affected, the days late or the amount misstated, and the supervisory impact.
Assign a root cause (calendar omission, late capital pack, tier misclassification, taxonomy version drift, unexplained non-blocking error, approval after submission) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where a reported ratio is misstated, open a resubmission and CFO-cleared notification to the NCA.
Carry every open issue into the next cycle's post-submission review as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has a filing issue with quantified impact, root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the review
actions: Compute the on-time submission rate, the blocking-error rate at submission and the tiering agreement rate, and compare each to the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside regulatory reporting production and prepared none of the tested filings, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, late filings and any restatement to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, submission and tiering rates, and an Audit Committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Runs the ORSA process and drafts the report under the Chief Risk Officer; the AMSB owns the assessment itself and cannot delegate the conclusion

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Solvency II Directive 2009/138/EC Art. 45(1) and Art. 246(4) for the group ORSA, with Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 262 and specifically Art. 262(1)(a) as amended by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/1256 requiring sustainability risks, including climate-change scenarios, in the assessment of overall solvency needs; re-read each ORSA cycle

In-scope processes.value: Risk identification and materiality assessment, overall solvency needs assessment, sustainability and climate scenario analysis, continuous compliance projection over the business plan, standard-formula deviation assessment, board challenge and approval, supervisory ORSA report

In-scope systems.value: Risk register, materiality scoring and the ORSA action log sit in the GRC platform; projections run in the actuarial modelling platform and the report is approved through the board portal

Compliance procedure documented.value: ORSA Policy and the ORSA Process Manual - trigger events for a non-regular ORSA, risk identification method, overall solvency needs methods, climate scenario set, projection basis, board challenge protocol and the supervisory report route

Compliance procedure approved.value: ORSA Policy approved by the AMSB annually; each ORSA report is approved by the AMSB before it is used in decision-making or sent to the supervisor

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: ORSA performed at least annually and immediately following any significant change in the risk profile; the supervisory ORSA report is submitted within two weeks of the conclusion of the assessment, so the board approval date starts a 14-day clock

Deadline reminders configured.value: The ORSA project plan alerts at T-90, T-60 and T-30 days to the scheduled board approval, and the GRC record auto-sets the supervisory submission task at board approval date +10 days

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Risk register extract, materiality scoring, scenario specifications and results, projection model runs, the actuarial function opinion, board papers and minutes, the approved ORSA report and the supervisory submission acknowledgement retained 10 years

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A missed annual cycle, a significant risk profile change without a triggered ORSA, an omitted climate scenario, or a late supervisory report is logged as a governance exception with root cause and owner

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs the ORSA report as complete and signs off closure of every ORSA action and every governance exception raised on the cycle

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every ORSA performed in the period (regular and triggered), the risk profile change events that could have triggered one, the scenario set run, and the ORSA actions raised

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance - a cycle with no ORSA, an ORSA report used without AMSB approval, a supervisory report later than two weeks after conclusion, or an overall solvency needs assessment with no sustainability and climate content is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is at least annual plus event-driven; the test runs annually after board approval with an interim check each quarter that no trigger event went without an ORSA

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside the risk function and must not have drafted any section of the tested ORSA report

Evidence location for test results.value: ORSA review workpaper (trigger analysis, scenario re-performance, projection recomputation, board challenge evidence, submission timing) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Approved ORSA report, the supporting scenario and projection packs, the actuarial function opinion and the board minutes evidencing challenge - producible for a supervisory ORSA review within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Chief Risk Officer leads supervisory dialogue on the ORSA with the Enterprise Risk Manager; the Regulatory Reporting Manager submits and tracks any follow-up information request

checklist.step: Open the ORSA cycle against the approved policy
actions: Read the ORSA Policy and confirm the scheduled cycle dates, the assessment reference date and the business plan version the projection will use.

Check the trigger list in the policy against the period's events - a major acquisition, a new line of business, a reinsurance programme change, a material reserve strengthening or a solvency ladder breach each force a non-regular ORSA.
Open the ORSA record in GRC with the reference date, the planned board approval date and the derived supervisory submission deadline at approval +14 days.
Issue the workplan to Actuarial, Capital Management, Finance, the Sustainability Risk Manager and the Chief Actuary with named deliverables and dates.
checklist.done: an ORSA record exists with reference date, planned approval date, derived submission deadline and a workplan with named deliverable owners.

checklist.step: Refresh the risk universe and materiality assessment
actions: Extract the risk register and re-score each risk for likelihood and impact with the risk owners, using the current exposure data rather than last year's scores.

Add risks that the standard formula does not capture - strategic risk, reputational risk, liquidity risk, group risk, sustainability risk, conduct risk, ICT and cyber concentration - and score them explicitly.
Set the materiality threshold as a quantified figure (for example a percentage of own funds) and record which risks fall above it, since those must be quantified in the overall solvency needs.
Record risks screened out as immaterial with the reason and the value tested, so the screening decision is auditable.
checklist.done: a re-scored risk register with a quantified materiality threshold, non-standard-formula risks scored, and screened-out risks reasoned.

checklist.step: Assess the overall solvency needs
actions: Quantify the capital needed for each material risk on the entity's own economic basis, stating the confidence level and time horizon used and why they differ from the SCR's 99.5% one-year basis where they do.
Quantify separately the risks the standard formula does not cover, and state the method for each - scenario, stress, factor or expert judgement with a documented rationale.
Aggregate to a single overall solvency needs figure showing the diversification assumed and its basis, and compare it to the SCR with the difference explained.
Record the expert judgements used, who made them and what evidence supported them, since these are the first thing a supervisor challenges.
checklist.done: an overall solvency needs figure exists on a stated basis, covering non-standard-formula risks, reconciled to the SCR with documented expert judgement.

checklist.step: Bring sustainability risks into the overall solvency needs
actions: Identify the material sustainability risks on both sides of the balance sheet: physical and transition climate risk in the underwriting portfolio, transition risk and stranded-asset risk in the investment portfolio, and litigation and conduct exposure.

Map the underwriting exposure by geography and peril with the CAT Modeler and the investment exposure by sector NACE code with the Investment Analyst, so the assessment rests on positions rather than narrative.
Assess each material sustainability risk for its effect on technical provisions, asset values and own funds and feed the quantification into the overall solvency needs.
Where a sustainability risk is judged immaterial, record the exposure tested and the threshold used - Art. 262(1)(a) as amended requires the consideration to be evidenced, not asserted.
checklist.done: material sustainability risks are identified from underwriting and investment positions and quantified into the overall solvency needs, with immateriality decisions evidenced.

checklist.step: Run the climate-change scenarios
actions: Specify at least two long-term climate scenarios where climate risk is material - one consistent with global temperature increase staying below 2 degrees and one where it exceeds 2 degrees - and state the reference pathway each is built on.
Run the physical-risk leg through the catastrophe model on the current underwriting portfolio with the frequency and severity uplifts the scenario implies, by peril and region.
Run the transition-risk leg on the investment portfolio with the Investment Analyst, applying sector-level valuation shocks and testing the carbon-intensive holdings individually.
Report the effect of each scenario on technical provisions, asset values, own funds and the projected solvency ratio over the scenario horizon, and state the management actions assumed.
checklist.done: at least two long-term climate scenarios are run on real portfolio positions with their solvency effect and assumed management actions stated.

checklist.step: Project continuous compliance with the SCR, MCR and technical provisions
actions: Project the balance sheet, own funds, SCR and MCR over the business plan horizon, typically three to five years, using the board-approved plan volumes, expenses and investment strategy.
Show projected SCR and MCR coverage at each year-end and confirm the entity would remain compliant continuously, not just at the endpoints.
Project the technical provisions on the same basis and confirm the assumptions used are consistent with those in the reserving and pricing work.
Flag any projected year where coverage falls below the board's appetite range and hand it to the Head of Capital Management for a management action.
checklist.done: a year-by-year projection of own funds, SCR, MCR and technical provisions over the plan horizon with any appetite breach flagged.

checklist.step: Assess deviation of the risk profile from the standard formula assumptions
actions: Compare the entity's actual risk profile module by module to the assumptions underlying the standard formula calibration - business mix, geographic concentration, reinsurance structure, asset allocation, catastrophe exposure.
Quantify the significance of each deviation and state whether the standard formula over- or under-states the capital need for that module.
Where a deviation is significant, set out the response: a USP application, a partial internal model, or a documented capital add-on to the overall solvency needs.
Record the conclusion as a clear statement on whether the standard formula remains appropriate for the entity.
checklist.done: a module-level deviation assessment with quantified significance and a stated conclusion on the appropriateness of the standard formula.

checklist.step: Run the stress and reverse stress tests supporting the assessment
actions: Run the single-factor sensitivities agreed with the Risk Committee - interest rates, spreads, equity, lapse, inflation, catastrophe - and report the coverage effect of each.
Run at least two combined-event scenarios that plausibly hit both sides of the balance sheet at once, since the standard formula's diversification is the assumption most likely to fail in practice.
Run the reverse stress test: find the combination of events that would exhaust eligible own funds against the SCR and describe how plausible it is.
Report each result with the recovery actions available, their lead times from the management action playbook, and the residual position after actions.
checklist.done: sensitivities, combined scenarios and a reverse stress test are run with coverage effects and post-action residual positions reported.

checklist.step: Set the capital plan and management actions arising
actions: Build the capital plan over the projection horizon showing planned issuance, redemptions, dividends and reinsurance changes against the projected requirement.
For each projected shortfall or appetite breach, name the management action, its coverage effect, its lead time and its owner, and test it against the playbook lead times.
Confirm with the Treasury Manager and the Chief Investment Officer that the assumed actions are executable in the assumed timeframe and market conditions.
Raise each action as an ORSA action in GRC with an owner and a due date rather than leaving it in the report narrative.
checklist.done: a capital plan covering the projection horizon with every shortfall answered by an owned, dated, executable action raised in GRC.

checklist.step: Draft the ORSA report
actions: Draft the report covering the assessment of overall solvency needs, continuous compliance with the SCR, MCR and technical provisions, and the significance of any deviation from the standard formula assumptions - the three assessments Art. 45(1) requires.
Include the sustainability and climate scenario section with the results, the assumptions and the limitations stated plainly.
State the methods, data, assumptions and expert judgements used, and the limitations of each, so the board can challenge them.
Set out the conclusions and the decisions the board is being asked to take, with each linked to an ORSA action.
checklist.done: a complete draft covering all three Art. 45(1) assessments plus climate scenarios, with methods, limitations and board decisions set out.

checklist.step: Obtain the actuarial function opinion
actions: Review the technical provisions, the underwriting policy and the reinsurance arrangements as they feed the ORSA and form the actuarial function's opinion on each.

Take sustainability risks into account in the opinion on the overall underwriting policy - state which sustainability risks were considered, how they bear on pricing, product design and portfolio steering, and what the conclusion is.
Where the opinion identifies a weakness, state the recommendation and the addressee rather than a general observation.
Sign and date the opinion and file it with the ORSA pack so the board sees it alongside the report.
checklist.done: a signed, dated actuarial function opinion covering technical provisions, underwriting policy including sustainability risks, and reinsurance.

checklist.step: Take the ORSA to the board for challenge and approval
actions: Circulate the ORSA report, the scenario pack, the capital plan and the actuarial function opinion at least 7 days before the meeting so the board can prepare challenge.
Run the session so the board actively steers the assessment - the AMSB is required to take an active part, not receive a finished product - and record the questions asked and the answers given.
Minute the approval of the ORSA report, the decisions taken on the capital plan and the date the assessment is concluded, since that date starts the 14-day supervisory clock.
Record any board-directed rework and re-table the affected section before approval rather than approving subject to changes.
checklist.done: minuted AMSB challenge, an approved report version, recorded decisions and an explicit assessment conclusion date.

checklist.step: Submit the supervisory ORSA report within two weeks
actions: Take the conclusion date from the board minutes and confirm the submission task is set at conclusion date +14 days at the latest.
Assemble the supervisory report package - the approved ORSA report, the scenario results and the actuarial function opinion where the NCA expects it - in the format the NCA specifies.
Submit through the supervisory channel, capture the acknowledgement id and record it against the GRC ORSA record.
Where the entity is part of a group, coordinate with the group risk function on whether a single group ORSA document is submitted under Art. 246(4) and record which entities it covers.
checklist.done: the supervisory ORSA report is submitted within two weeks of the board conclusion date with an acknowledgement id recorded.

checklist.step: Embed the ORSA into decision-making
actions: Feed the ORSA conclusions into the business plan, the reinsurance strategy, the investment mandate and the product pricing reviews, and record where each conclusion landed.
Track every ORSA action to closure in GRC with monthly reporting to the Risk Committee on overdue actions.
Re-open the ORSA where a trigger event occurs before the next scheduled cycle, using the same process on the changed risk profile.
Review at the next cycle whether the prior year's actions changed behaviour, and report that assessment to the board.
checklist.done: each ORSA conclusion is traceable to a business decision, actions are tracked to closure, and prior-year effectiveness is reported.

checklist.step: Retain the ORSA evidence
actions: Archive the risk register extract, materiality scoring, scenario specifications and results, projection runs with their model versions, the capital plan, the actuarial function opinion, the board papers and minutes, the approved report and the acknowledgement.
Index by ORSA reference date and entity, and cross-link triggered ORSAs to the event that triggered them.
Apply the 10-year retention label and confirm the archive is searchable by reference date, scenario name and action id.
Confirm with the Enterprise Risk Manager that the archived report version is the board-approved version number.
checklist.done: a complete, labelled and searchable ORSA archive holding the board-approved version and all supporting runs.

testing.step: Build the population of ORSA cycles and trigger events
actions: List every ORSA record in the period by entity, with its reference date, conclusion date and submission date.

Independently build the list of events that the ORSA Policy defines as triggers - acquisitions, new lines of business, reinsurance programme changes, material reserve movements, solvency ladder breaches - from board minutes, the breach register and the change log.
Match trigger events to triggered ORSAs and list every event with no ORSA behind it as a completeness exception.
testing.done: a full ORSA inventory matched to an independently built trigger event list, with unmatched triggers listed.

testing.step: Reconcile the ORSA inputs to the source of record
actions: Agree the opening balance sheet, own funds and SCR in the projection to the CFO-signed capital pack for the reference date.
Agree the projection's volumes, expenses and investment strategy to the board-approved business plan version named in the report.
Agree the underwriting and investment exposures used in the climate scenarios to the portfolio extracts and the custodian position report.
Clear every difference before sampling.
testing.done: projection openings, plan assumptions and scenario exposures all tie to signed source records with differences cleared.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of ORSA cycles in the period and 100% of climate scenarios run.
Take 15 material risks by seeded random selection from the risk register, forced to include every risk not covered by the standard formula.
Record the seed, population sizes and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all ORSA cycles, all climate scenarios and every non-standard-formula risk.

testing.step: Re-perform the materiality screening and solvency needs quantification
actions: Take the quantified materiality threshold and re-apply it to the risk register yourself, before reading which risks were carried into the overall solvency needs.
For each sampled material risk, re-perform or inspect the quantification and confirm the method, confidence level and horizon stated in the report match what was actually run.
Test the expert judgements: confirm each names the person, the evidence and the date, and challenge any judgement with no supporting analysis.
Treat a risk screened out as immaterial without a tested value as an exception.
testing.done: materiality screening is independently re-applied and each sampled risk's quantification is traced to a run matching the stated method.

testing.step: Test the sustainability and climate scenario content
actions: Confirm at least two long-term scenarios were run where climate risk is material, one below and one above 2 degrees, with the reference pathway named for each.
Re-run one physical-risk scenario on the same portfolio extract and compare the modelled loss to the reported figure.
Confirm the transition-risk leg was applied to actual investment holdings by sector rather than to an index proxy, and inspect the treatment of the largest carbon-intensive holdings.
Treat a report that discusses climate risk without a quantified portfolio-level result as a fail against Art. 262(1)(a) as amended.
testing.done: both required scenarios are evidenced with named pathways, one physical scenario is re-run and agrees, and transition shocks hit real holdings.

testing.step: Recompute the continuous compliance projection
actions: Rebuild the own funds and SCR projection for two plan years independently from the plan assumptions and compare to the reported path.
Confirm coverage was assessed at every projected year-end and not only at the horizon, and that the MCR was projected as well as the SCR.
Test whether any projected year breaches the board appetite and, where it does, confirm the report says so rather than smoothing it.
Confirm the technical provisions projection uses assumptions consistent with the reserving basis.
testing.done: two projection years are independently rebuilt and agree, with year-by-year coverage and any appetite breach disclosed.

testing.step: Test the standard formula deviation assessment
actions: For each material module, compare the entity's actual business mix, concentration and reinsurance structure to the standard formula calibration assumptions yourself.
Confirm the report quantifies the significance of each deviation rather than describing it qualitatively.
Where a significant deviation is identified, confirm a response is stated - USP application, partial internal model or an add-on to overall solvency needs - with an owner and a date.
Treat a blanket statement that the standard formula is appropriate, with no module-level analysis, as a fail.
testing.done: each material module has an evidenced deviation analysis with quantified significance and, where significant, an owned response.

testing.step: Trace board challenge, approval and the two-week submission clock
actions: Read the board minutes and evidence active challenge - recorded questions, answers and any directed rework - not merely a resolution to approve.
Take the conclusion date from the minutes and recompute the supervisory submission deadline as conclusion date plus two weeks.
Compare the recomputed deadline to the submission timestamp on the NCA acknowledgement and quantify any lateness in days.
Confirm the version submitted is the version the board approved, by version number and page count.
testing.done: board challenge is evidenced from the minutes, the 14-day clock is recomputed from the conclusion date and the submitted version matches the approved one.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception with the entity, ORSA reference date, the requirement missed and the supervisory impact.

Assign a root cause (trigger event not recognised, materiality threshold not applied, climate scenario narrative-only, projection not year-by-year, approval without recorded challenge, late submission) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where the supervisory report was late or incomplete, agree the notification wording with the Chief Risk Officer before it goes to the NCA.
Carry every open issue into the next ORSA cycle's review as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has a GRC issue with root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the review
actions: State whether all three Art. 45(1) assessments and the Art. 262(1)(a) sustainability requirement were met, and compute the trigger-event coverage rate.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside the risk function and drafted no section of the report, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Audit Committee and the AMSB and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper stating a conclusion against each Art. 45(1) assessment, the trigger coverage rate and board reporting dates.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual stress and scenario testing programme and the SFCR Section C risk-profile disclosure; the Chief Actuary owns the underwriting and reserving scenarios inside it

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 295 requiring the SFCR to describe, separately for underwriting, market, credit, liquidity, operational and other material risks, the exposure, concentration, mitigation and sensitivity including the results of stress and scenario testing; re-read at the start of each annual SFCR cycle

In-scope processes.value: Stress and scenario programme design, per-risk-category scenario calibration and execution (underwriting, market, credit, liquidity, operational, other), reverse stress testing, results aggregation and the SFCR Section C drafting

In-scope systems.value: Scenario runs execute in the actuarial modelling platform with catastrophe scenarios in Moody's RMS and market shocks sourced from Bloomberg; the programme and results are logged in the GRC platform and published through the SFCR

Compliance procedure documented.value: Stress and Scenario Testing Policy plus the annual programme document - the scenario library by risk category, calibration basis, run calendar, management action assumptions, reporting route and the SFCR Section C mapping

Compliance procedure approved.value: Policy approved by the AMSB annually; the annual programme and the scenario set are approved by the Risk Committee before the runs start

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: The programme runs annually so results are available for the ORSA and for SFCR Section C, which itself is due within 14 weeks of year-end for solo entities and 20 weeks for the group; any supervisory or EIOPA stress test exercise runs to the deadlines in its own technical specifications

Deadline reminders configured.value: The programme plan alerts at T-60 and T-30 days to the results deadline for the ORSA and at T-45 days to the SFCR Section C drafting cut-off, with the Chief Risk Officer copied on slips

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Scenario specifications with calibration sources, model run logs and versions, per-category results packs, management action assumptions, Risk Committee minutes and the SFCR Section C source file retained 10 years

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A risk category with no scenario run, an uncalibrated or unapproved scenario, a result not reflected in SFCR Section C, or a management action assumed without a playbook entry is logged as an exception with owner and disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs the results pack and confirms every scenario finding is either reflected in SFCR Section C or explicitly closed with a reason

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every scenario in the approved annual programme across the six risk categories, their model runs, and the SFCR Section C sensitivity statements built from them

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on category coverage - any of underwriting, market, credit, liquidity, operational or other material risk lacking a run scenario and a disclosed sensitivity is a fail; any SFCR sensitivity figure that does not tie to a model run is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual through the SFCR; the test runs annually before SFCR sign-off with a mid-year check that the programme is on schedule

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have specified, calibrated or run any scenario in the tested programme

Evidence location for test results.value: Stress testing review workpaper (category coverage matrix, calibration re-performance, run reconciliation, SFCR tie-out, exceptions) in the model governance repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Approved programme document, scenario specifications with calibration sources, results packs by risk category and the SFCR Section C tie-out - producible for a supervisory review of the risk profile disclosure within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Chief Risk Officer answers supervisory questions on scenario design and results; the Regulatory Reporting Manager handles any EIOPA or NCA stress test data request and its resubmissions

checklist.step: Set the annual stress and scenario programme
actions: Draft the programme listing, for each of the six Art. 295 categories - underwriting, market, credit, liquidity, operational and other material risks - the scenarios to be run, their owner, their model and their run date.
Build the coverage matrix that maps every scenario to the risk category and the SFCR Section C sub-section it will feed, so a category cannot silently go unrun.
Set the results deadline back from the ORSA board date and the SFCR Section C drafting cut-off.
Take the programme to the Risk Committee for approval and record the approval date and any scenario the committee added or removed.
checklist.done: a Risk-Committee-approved programme with a coverage matrix showing at least one owned, dated scenario for each of the six categories.

checklist.step: Specify and calibrate each scenario
actions: Write a one-page specification per scenario: the narrative, the shocked variables with their magnitudes, the time horizon, the balance-sheet items affected and the metrics to be reported.
State the calibration basis for each shock - a historical event, a statistical return period, a supervisory prescribed shock or expert judgement - and name the source document.
Set the severity so it is plausible but severe: scenarios calibrated to a mild return period produce disclosures that tell a supervisor nothing.
Have the Chief Risk Officer approve each specification before the run, and version-control it so results can be tied back to the exact specification used.
checklist.done: every scenario has a versioned, CRO-approved specification naming its shocked variables, magnitudes, horizon and calibration source.

checklist.step: Calibrate the market risk shocks
actions: Pull from Bloomberg the historical series for government yields by tenor, credit spreads by rating band, equity indices, property indices and FX rates over at least the last 20 years.
Derive the shock magnitudes at the chosen return period and cross-check them against the standard formula shocks so the report can explain where the internal scenario is more or less severe.
Specify combined market scenarios - a rates-down with spreads-wide and equity-down combination, and an inflation-shock combination - since single-factor moves understate the balance-sheet effect.
Hand the calibrated shocks to the Capital Model Actuary with the derivation workbook attached.
checklist.done: market shocks are derived from a named historical window at a stated return period, cross-checked to the standard formula, and handed over with the derivation.

checklist.step: Run the catastrophe and underwriting scenarios
actions: Run the natural catastrophe scenarios on the current exposure file - windstorm, flood, earthquake and wildfire as relevant to the portfolio - at the return periods the specification sets.
Report gross and net of reinsurance losses, showing the reinstatement premiums and the retention and limit consumed on each treaty, taken from the treaty repository.
Run a second-event scenario after the first has consumed reinsurance, since the eroded programme is where the real exposure sits.
Add man-made scenarios where material - a single large liability loss, a cyber accumulation event - and state the accumulation assumption used.
checklist.done: catastrophe and man-made scenarios are run on the current exposure file with gross, net, reinstatement and second-event results reported.

checklist.step: Run the reserving and premium deterioration scenarios
actions: Run the reserve deterioration scenario by applying the specified uplift to the best estimate by line of business and re-deriving the technical provisions and the risk margin.
Run an inflation scenario on claims severity, showing the effect on long-tail lines separately since they carry the duration.
Run a premium adequacy scenario reflecting a soft-market rate reduction and loss ratio deterioration over the plan horizon.
Report the effect of each on technical provisions, own funds and the non-life underwriting module of the SCR.
checklist.done: reserve, inflation and premium adequacy scenarios are run with their effect on technical provisions, own funds and the SCR reported by line of business.

checklist.step: Run the credit and counterparty default scenarios
actions: Run the default of the single largest reinsurance counterparty, taking the recoverable balance and any collateral held from the ceded accounting platform and the treaty repository.
Run a systemic downgrade scenario moving all counterparties down one to two credit quality steps and re-derive the counterparty default charge.
Run a corporate bond default and downgrade scenario on the investment portfolio with the Investment Analyst, applying migration to the holdings by rating band.
Report the combined effect on own funds and on the counterparty default and spread risk modules.
checklist.done: counterparty default, systemic downgrade and bond migration scenarios are run from actual exposures with their module effects reported.

checklist.step: Run the liquidity stress scenario
actions: Build the stressed cash-flow projection over 1 week, 1 month, 3 months and 12 months combining a catastrophe claims outflow, a mass lapse or surrender outflow and a collateral call on derivative positions.

Classify the asset portfolio into liquidity buckets in Aladdin, applying haircuts by asset class and testing whether the assets can actually be sold in the stressed window rather than assuming they can.
Compute the liquidity coverage in each horizon and identify the first horizon at which the buffer fails.
Report the available contingent funding - repo lines, committed facilities, intra-group support - with the time it takes to draw each.
checklist.done: a stressed cash-flow projection across four horizons with haircut-adjusted asset liquidity, a stated failure point and drawable contingent funding.

checklist.step: Run the operational and ICT scenarios
actions: Build scenarios against the identified critical or important functions: a prolonged outage of the policy administration platform, a ransomware event on the claims platform, and the failure of a critical ICT third-party provider.
Quantify the loss using the impact tolerance for each function, the operational loss database and the cost drivers - recovery costs, regulatory penalty exposure, client redress and lost business.

Test the scenarios against the business continuity and disaster recovery test results supplied by the Business Continuity Manager, so the assumed recovery time is one that has actually been demonstrated.
Report the effect on own funds and compare it to the standard formula operational risk charge, stating whether the charge looks adequate.
checklist.done: operational and ICT scenarios are quantified against impact tolerances and demonstrated recovery times, and compared to the SCR_op charge.

checklist.step: Run the reverse stress test
actions: Define the failure point to be searched for - eligible own funds falling below the SCR, and separately below the MCR - and work backwards to the combinations of events that reach it.
Produce at least two distinct paths to failure with different dominant drivers, so the exercise does not simply restate the largest single risk.
Assess the plausibility of each path and name the early-warning indicators that would show it developing, and hand those indicators to the Risk Analyst for the monitoring dashboard.
Take the reverse stress results to the Risk Committee with a recommendation on which vulnerabilities need a management action.
checklist.done: at least two distinct failure paths are identified with plausibility assessments, early-warning indicators and a committee recommendation.

checklist.step: Run the scenarios through the capital model consistently
actions: Run every scenario off the same frozen data cut and the same model version, recording the run id and model version for each so results are comparable and reproducible.

For each scenario report the effect on assets, technical provisions, own funds by tier, the SCR, the MCR and both coverage ratios - a scenario reported only as a loss figure cannot feed a sensitivity disclosure.
State whether management actions are assumed in each result and report pre-action and post-action figures separately.
Log every run in the model run log with its specification version so a result can be traced to the specification it came from.
checklist.done: every scenario is run on one frozen data cut and model version, reporting pre- and post-action effects on own funds, SCR, MCR and coverage.

checklist.step: Participate in the supervisory or EIOPA stress test exercise
actions: Read the exercise technical specifications and the Q and A when the NCA or EIOPA launches an exercise, and map each requested data field to an internal source before any work starts.
Run the prescribed scenarios exactly as specified, including where the prescribed shocks differ from the internal calibration - never substitute the internal scenario.
Complete the submission templates, validate them, obtain the sign-off the specification requires (usually the AMSB or the CRO) and submit by the exercise deadline with the acknowledgement captured.
Track and answer the follow-up queries and any resubmission request, and file the final submitted templates alongside the internal programme results.
checklist.done: any launched exercise is run on prescribed shocks, submitted by its deadline with the required sign-off, and the templates are filed.

checklist.step: Aggregate the results and set the management actions
actions: Build the results dashboard showing each scenario's coverage effect side by side, ranked by severity, with the risk category tagged.
Identify the scenarios that would take coverage below the board's appetite range and, for each, name the management action, its coverage effect and its lead time from the playbook.
Confirm with the Treasury Manager and the Head of Reinsurance that each assumed action is executable in the scenario's own conditions - a rights issue in a market-wide stress is not.
Raise each required action in GRC with an owner and a due date and report the set to the Risk Committee.
checklist.done: a ranked results dashboard with an owned, dated and feasibility-tested management action for every appetite-breaching scenario.

checklist.step: Draft SFCR Section C from the results
actions: Draft Section C with a separate sub-section for underwriting, market, credit, liquidity, operational and other material risks, as Art. 295 requires - do not merge categories.

In each sub-section state the exposure measure, the material concentrations, the risk mitigation techniques used and their effectiveness, and the sensitivity including the stress and scenario results.

Quote the actual scenario results as figures with the shock described, so a reader can see the severity tested; for liquidity, include the expected profit included in future premiums where the disclosure requires it.
Tie every figure in Section C to a named model run id in the tie-out schedule attached to the drafting file.
checklist.done: Section C has all six sub-sections with exposure, concentration, mitigation and quantified sensitivity, every figure tied to a named run id.

checklist.step: Take the results and disclosure to the Risk Committee and board
actions: Table the results pack, the reverse stress conclusions, the management actions and the draft Section C at the Risk Committee, and record the challenge in the minutes.
Confirm the board sees the same severity in Section C as it saw in the results pack - a disclosure softened after the committee saw the numbers is a governance finding.
Obtain the board's decisions on any risk appetite change, de-risking action or reinsurance purchase arising, with owners and dates.
Feed the approved Section C to the Regulatory Reporting Manager for inclusion in the SFCR.
checklist.done: minuted committee and board challenge on the results, decisions with owners, and an approved Section C consistent with the results pack.

checklist.step: Retain the scenario evidence
actions: Archive per scenario: the versioned specification, the calibration workbook and its data source, the model run log entry with run id and model version, the results pack and the management action record.
Archive the coverage matrix, the Risk Committee approval of the programme and the Section C tie-out schedule alongside them.
Apply the 10-year retention label and confirm the archive is searchable by scenario name, risk category, run id and reporting year.
Reconcile the archived scenario count to the approved programme and chase any scenario in the programme with no archived result.
checklist.done: every programme scenario has an archived specification, calibration, run and result, reconciled to the approved programme with no gaps.

testing.step: Build the population of programme scenarios and runs
actions: Extract the Risk-Committee-approved programme with every scenario, its risk category, owner and planned run date.
Extract the model run log for the year and list every run tagged to a scenario, including re-runs and abandoned runs.
Match programme to runs and list every approved scenario with no completed run, and every run with no approved specification, before sampling.
testing.done: the approved programme is matched to actual runs with unrun scenarios and unapproved runs both listed.

testing.step: Test coverage of all six Art. 295 risk categories
actions: Build a coverage matrix independently from the regulation text: underwriting, market, credit, liquidity, operational and other material risks.
Map each completed run to a category and identify any category with no run scenario or with only a qualitative treatment.
Confirm each category's SFCR sub-section exists and contains a quantified sensitivity, not a narrative statement.
Treat any uncovered category as a fail regardless of how many scenarios were run elsewhere.
testing.done: every one of the six categories has at least one completed quantitative scenario mapped to a populated SFCR sub-section.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of the scenarios whose results are quoted in SFCR Section C and 100% of the reverse stress paths.
Take 10 further scenarios by seeded random selection across the remaining programme, forced to include at least one from each category.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering every disclosed scenario, the reverse stress paths and at least one scenario per category.

testing.step: Reconcile the runs to a single frozen data cut and model version
actions: For each sampled run, take the run id and confirm the input data cut and model version match the base capital run for the reference date.
Confirm the unstressed base result in each scenario pack equals the reported base own funds, SCR and coverage - a base that does not tie means the scenario is not comparable.
List any scenario run on a different data cut or model version and assess whether the results in Section C are therefore inconsistent.
testing.done: every sampled run ties to the same frozen data cut and model version and reproduces the reported base position.

testing.step: Re-perform the calibration of the sampled scenarios
actions: Take the calibration source named in each sampled specification and re-derive the shock magnitude yourself from the same historical window and return period.
Compare the internal shock to the standard formula shock for the same risk and confirm the report explains any case where the internal scenario is materially milder.
Challenge expert-judgement calibrations that have no analysis behind them and any severity that was reduced between specification versions.
Confirm the specification version referenced in the results pack is the version the Chief Risk Officer approved.
testing.done: each sampled shock is independently re-derived from its named source and any softening between specification versions is identified.

testing.step: Re-perform two scenario results end to end
actions: Select one market and one underwriting or catastrophe scenario and re-run them from the specification on the frozen data cut.
Compare the resulting effect on own funds, SCR, MCR and coverage to the reported figures and explain any difference above 1%.
Confirm the pre-action and post-action results are reported separately and that the management actions applied match the approved playbook entries.
Confirm net-of-reinsurance catastrophe results reflect the actual treaty structure including reinstatements and eroded limits.
testing.done: two scenarios are re-run end to end and agree to the reported effects within 1%, with action assumptions traced to the playbook.

testing.step: Test the liquidity and operational scenarios against demonstrated capability
actions: For the liquidity scenario, test the asset liquidity haircuts and bucket assignments against actual trade data or the custodian's liquidity classification, and challenge any asset assumed saleable within a week that has no recent trading history.
Confirm the contingent funding assumed is committed and drawable in the stated timeframe by reading the facility agreements.
For the operational scenarios, compare the assumed recovery times to the latest BCP and DR test results and treat any assumed recovery faster than the demonstrated one as an exception.
Confirm the operational scenario loss estimates draw on the operational loss database rather than only on expert opinion.
testing.done: liquidity haircuts, funding availability and operational recovery times are all supported by trade data, facility terms and demonstrated test results.

testing.step: Tie SFCR Section C to the model runs
actions: Take every quantified sensitivity figure in Section C and trace it through the tie-out schedule to a named run id and results pack.
Confirm the shock described in the disclosure matches the shock in the specification - a disclosure quoting a milder shock than was run, or a result from a different scenario, is a misstatement.
Confirm each sub-section states exposure, concentration, mitigation and sensitivity as Art. 295 requires, and that mitigation effectiveness is evidenced.
Compare the severity presented to the board in the results pack to the severity in the published Section C and flag any softening.
testing.done: every Section C figure traces to a named run with a matching shock description, and no softening between the board pack and the disclosure.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception with the scenario name, risk category, the requirement missed and whether the SFCR disclosure is affected.
Assign a root cause (category not covered, scenario unrun, calibration unsupported, mixed data cuts, unexecutable management action assumed, disclosure not tied to a run) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where a published Section C figure is wrong, open a correction assessment with the Regulatory Reporting Manager and the Chief Financial Officer.
Carry every open issue into next year's programme review as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has a GRC issue with root cause, owner, remediation date, disclosure impact and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the review
actions: State the category coverage rate across the six Art. 295 categories and the proportion of Section C figures successfully tied to a model run.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who specified, calibrated and ran none of the tested scenarios, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any disclosure misstatement to the Risk Committee and the Audit Committee before the SFCR is approved, and file the workpaper in the model governance repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, category coverage and tie-out rates, reported before SFCR approval and filed in the repository.
